extension was never built.","quote":"it tries the compiled `_speedups._escape_inner` and falls back to the pure-Python `_native._escape_inner` if the C extension was never built"},{"claim":"The `_speedups._escape_inner` and `_native._escape_inner` implementations have identical behaviour and differ only in speed.","quote":"Whichever one it got, the behaviour is the same; only the speed differs."},{"claim":"The module-level `escape` function begins with an identity check `type(s) is str` rather than `isinstance(s, str)`.","quote":"`escape` begins with a single identity check"},{"claim":"A comment in `markupsafe/__init__.py` explains that a proxy object can report a borrowed `__class__`, so `isinstance(s, str)` can return `True` for a non-string.","quote":"a proxy object can report a borrowed `__class__`, so `isinstance(s, str)` can be made to return `True` for something that is not a string at all"},{"claim":"In `escape`, an object that is not exactly `str` falls through to the later branches instead of the fast path.","quote":"so a proxy falls through to the slower, more careful branches instead of being waved past"},{"claim":"In `_native.py`, `_escape_inner` is implemented as five chained `str.replace` calls.","quote":"In the Python implementation it is five chained `str.replace` calls"},{"claim":"`_native._escape_inner` replaces `&` with `&` first, then `>`, `<`, `'`, and `\"`.","quote":"`&` → `&`, then `>`, `<`, `'`, `\"`"},{"claim":"In `_native._escape_inner`, `&` is replaced first because the other four replacements introduce new `&` characters.","quote":"`&` is replaced *first*, because the other four replacements all introduce new `&` characters"},{"claim":"The C implementation in `_speedups.c` performs the same five replacements in one pass with the output sized ahead of time.","quote":"The C version does the same five, in one pass, sized ahead of time"},{"claim":"In `_speedups.c`, if the scan finds nothing to escape it increments the refcount and returns the same string object.","quote":"if the scan finds nothing to escape it increments the refcount and hands back the *same* string object"},{"claim":"`_speedups.c` dispatches the escape routine by string width.","quote":"dispatched by width at"},{"claim":"MarkupSafe's escaping covers exactly five characters: `&`, `>`, `<`, `'`, and `\"`.","quote":"Five characters is the entire scope of the escaping: `& > < ' \"`"},{"claim":"MarkupSafe's escaping does not touch backtick, `=`, or whitespace.","quote":"Backtick, `=`, and whitespace are not touched."},{"claim":"In `escape`, the escaped text is passed to the `Markup` constructor.","quote":"The escaped text is handed to `Markup(...)`"},{"claim":"`Markup.__new__` accepts parameters `object`, `encoding` defaulting to `None`, and `errors` defaulting to `'strict'`.","quote":"`object='<script>alert(document.cookie);</script>', encoding=None, errors='strict'`"},{"claim":"`Markup.__new__` performs no escaping.","quote":"`Markup.__new__` performs no escaping whatsoever"},{"claim":"`Markup.__new__` checks whether the object has an `__html__` method and, if so, uses its return value.","quote":"It checks whether the object has an `__html__` method and, if so, uses its return value"},{"claim":"When `encoding` is `None`, `Markup.__new__` calls `str.__new__` and returns.","quote":"since `encoding` is `None` here — it calls `str.__new__` and returns"},{"claim":"`Markup.__new__` has a bytes-decoding branch where `encoding` and `errors` are forwarded.","quote":"The bytes-decoding road, where `encoding` and `errors` are forwarded"},{"claim":"The `Markup` class defines `__slots__ = ()`.","quote":"The class carries `__slots__ = ()`"},{"claim":"`Markup.__repr__` wraps `str.__repr__` output in the class name.","quote":"`__repr__` wraps `str.__repr__` in the class name"},{"claim":"`Markup` is a subclass of `str`, so `type(s) is str` is `False` for a `Markup` instance in `escape`.","quote":"`Markup` is a subclass of `str`, so `type(s) is str` is `False` and the fast path is refused"},{"claim":"The second branch of `escape` is a `hasattr(s, \"__html__\")` check.","quote":"The next check, `hasattr(s, \"__html__\")`, succeeds"},{"claim":"`Markup.__html__` returns `self`.","quote":"`Markup.__html__` simply returns `self`"},{"claim":"Escaping a `Markup` value does not run the five replacements, so `<` does not become `&lt;`.","quote":"The five replacements never run. `<` does not become re-checks for `__html__` on the value it was handed"},{"claim":"The third branch of `escape` is `Markup(_escape_inner(str(s)))`.","quote":"would fall to the third branch,
